title: Quantization profile lifecycle: FP8/INT8 calibration, canary rollout, and automated fallback policy
creator: Priya Natarajan
description:
Goal: Add a robust lifecycle for quantization profiles (FP8 and INT8) that ties automated calibration and accuracy validation into a safe canary rollout with deterministic automatic fallback when quality checks fail. Context: Teams want to ship quantized model variants to reduce cost while avoiding regressions in user-facing metrics. We need a repeatable flow: calibration -> offline validation -> canary traffic -> live metric gating -> automated rollback/fallback to higher-precision variant if quality drops.

Scope:
- Define canonical quantization profile metadata and storage format for FP8/INT8 (including per-layer, per-op config and calibration seed).
- Implement a calibration job template (batchable) that produces candidate profiles and calibration stats (KL histograms, per-tensor max, activation ranges).
- Create an accuracy validation harness that runs candidate profiles against representative eval sets (classification, perplexity, NLL, task-specific metrics) and produces a quality report.
- Build canary rollout orchestration: route a small percent of production traffic to quantized variant, collect metrics, run statistical tests, promote or trigger fallback.
- Implement automatic fallback policy: deterministic criteria (metric thresholds + statistical significance + sample size) to switch routing to a compatible fallback model (higher-precision or unquantized) within SLOs.

Non-goals: automated retraining, per-customer custom datasets (will follow-up as separate initiative).
acceptance_criteria: A calibration job produces a reusable quantization profile artifact with schema version and hash
"Accuracy validation report" is created automatically and stored with the profile (includes top-line metrics and downgrade reasons)
Canary rollout can be initiated from Console with a 0.1% to 5% traffic window and a configurable duration
If any configured quality gate fails, the router switches traffic to fallback model within 30s and an alert is emitted
Metrics and traces for the canary period are available in Console dashboard and in the canary report link
implementation_notes: Quantization artifact format: JSON manifest with model_id, base_model_version, quant_profile_id, schema_version, calibration_stats_url, validation_report_url, compatible_fallbacks list
Calibration job will run on a small GPU fleet with deterministic RNG seed; store the seed to reproduce calibration
Calibration outputs: per-layer scale/zero-point, fused-op ranges, KL divergence per-activation histogram, outlier counts
Validation harness must support multiple evaluation modes: offline sample eval, streaming A/B style sim, and synthetic stress tests for tails
Canary controller integrates with smart routing layer; it must be able to fallback to a compatible model variant (e.g., fp16 or fp32) preserving tokenization and response format
Rollout policy uses sequential checks: warmup traffic collection -> primary metric tests -> secondary metric checks -> approval or rollback
Primary metrics recommended: task accuracy (or BLEU/ROUGE for seq2seq), response quality score, end-to-end latency impact, 99th percentile latency, token error rate where applicable
Statistical test: sequential probability ratio test (SPRT) with minimum sample size 5000 in canary window, or bootstrap CI if small samples
Fallback mechanism: router publishes pre-signed update event to control plane which executes within 30s and logs to audit trail
Console: expose a canary report link with pass/fail, metric deltas, and a link to the calibration artifact and validation report
risks: False positives: noise in low-traffic canaries could trigger unnecessary rollbacks
Calibration nondeterminism if RNG seeds or aten kernels differ across infra; need strict reproducibility
Model compatibility: some quantized variants change output distribution in subtle ways that break downstream parsers
Latency regressions from dequantization paths or padding changes in kernels
Operational complexity: supporting many quant profiles per model increases storage and routing complexity
plan: Week 1: finalize quant_profile manifest schema and calibration job template; prototype with BERT-family model for INT8
Week 2: implement validation harness and baseline eval sets; run calibration + validation on small models and collect baseline reports
Week 3: implement canary controller integration with routing and console UI for initiating canary
Week 4: automated fallback logic, alerting, and audit logging; end-to-end integration tests
Week 5: staged rollout internally and to selected customer beta; iterate on thresholds and metrics
Week 6: GA gates, docs, runbook, and postmortem drill scripts
progress_updates: 2026-02-22: Kickoff sync with Serving, Runtime, and Console owners. Agreed schema should include calibration_stats_url and compatible_fallbacks.
2026-03-01: Prototype calibration job completed for bert-small-int8; generated quant_profile v1 (artifact hash: qpf_v1_9f3c).

2026-03-04: Validation harness ran on representative eval set (SQuAD+GLUE subset). Observed 0.9% drop in F1 for int8 profile; captured full validation report: drive.redwood/drive/validation/ENG-8423/bert-small-int8-report.pdf
2026-03-06: Design review with Console team about canary UX. Decided to support quick launch presets (0.1%, 1%, 5%) and custom window durations.

2026-03-09: Routing prototype accepts fallback list and can swap to fallback model id within 22s in dev cluster. Recorded issue: race condition when two concurrent canaries run for same model (ENG-8501).
2026-03-12: Implemented basic automated gating using SPRT with alpha=0.01, beta=0.05 and min_samples=5000. Running medium-scale canary on internal traffic tomorrow.
open_questions: What should the default gating thresholds be across different model classes (chat vs embed vs LLM)? Suggestion: stricter for chat (max 0.5% absolute accuracy drop) and laxer for embeddings (cosine shift < 0.01)
How to handle per-customer custom prompts that reveal quantization regressions not captured by shared eval sets? (deferred to PM roadmap)
Should we allow dynamic adjustment of canary size based on early metric drift signals? (requires additional safety checks)
Do we expose a manual 'force promote' in Console and how to require approvers for that action?
